name: Ferrochem AcidWall Shelf Hazmat Rig MK-2
description:
A full-enclosure hazmat suit built for Shelf-zone acid rain and industrial chemical exposure. Outer shell is laminated PVC-nitrile composite in oxidized amber — a color chosen because it hides staining. Seams are triple-welded with butyl tape reinforcement; most suits show darkened stress lines around the wrists and collar from repeated decontamination cycling. Hood integrates a polycarbonate visor with anti-fog coating that usually starts failing after six months.

Inner layer is a moisture-wicking mesh bonded to a thin neoprene barrier. Boot covers are fused to the leg panels — no separate footwear required. Designed for single-occupational-tier users who cannot afford replacements on schedule.
functionality: Full chemical splash and acid rain protection rated to pH 1.5. Integrated boot covers. Visor provides basic HUD mounting rail. Pressure-release valves at wrists allow limited aug cable routing. Rated for 40-hour continuous wear before mandatory decon.
what_it_says: You work where the air tries to kill you and you can't afford to stop.
story_hooks: A worker's suit has a hand-written serial number crossed out and replaced — it's been passed down through three people, two of whom didn't make it.
Someone has been leaving deactivated suits propped upright in contaminated zones — twelve so far, each containing a folded note.
A batch of MK-2s were sold with a manufacturing defect in the butyl seam tape — someone is quietly buying them back before the failure rate becomes a story.
